candidates.what: Verso (image 2): alphabet-correspondence table. About 14 Arabic letters in rows (alif ba jim dal ... kaf lam mim nun sin ayn fa ... shin) each with a small invented/Coptic-Greek-like numeral or sign written beneath, plus a few Western digits (3,5) and a short line at foot. PGP says it is a table of Greek/Coptic numerals against Arabic letters. Looks like a key/cipher alphabet or numeral table; no running text on this side; recto is recipes.

Pen-trial sheet (image 2). Top left: a ruled box with 4 rows of about 8 invented signs each (hooks, crosses, Hebrew/Greek-like shapes), not Hebrew or Arabic. Right: Hebrew alphabet strings (atbash-like 'atbshr...', abjad order, tally strokes) and odd letter strings, with Arabic jottings. PGP: pen trials, Hebrew alphabets in abjad order. The boxed sign grid and alphabet drills could be a secret script or key; unclear.

Verso (image 2) of a Judaeo-Arabic letter: address plus 'random jottings'. About 8 lines of word-like groups in angular Greek/Coptic-looking and Hebrew-shaped letters (L, Г, Ш, square forms), 12-25 signs per line, many words starting with alef; also triangle signs and a block 'ה י ל ו ל ה / אאבם ...' laid out like a magic square; Hebrew spell names. Could be a cipher text, a pen-trial or magical letter strings; cannot tell. Weak A.

Probably magical letter strings (charakteres-like); no key; not shown to be a cipher.
